subject: Agriculture
title: Seed Patents and Ownership
description: A micro-lesson that makes Seed Patents and Ownership usable.

hook.text: Four companies control 60% of the global seed market. Seeds that were once shared freely are now patented products.

buildup.text: Bayer-Monsanto, Corteva, Syngenta, and BASF dominate. Farmers must buy new seeds each season.

discovery.text: Patent laws prohibit farmers from saving and replanting patented seeds—a practice that sustained agriculture for 10,000 years.

twist.text: Monsanto sued hundreds of farmers for patent infringement—even when wind blew patented pollen onto their fields.

climax.text: The Open Source Seed Initiative is creating 'unpatentable' seeds—freely available, like open-source software.

punchline.text: Seeds were humanity's shared tech. Now they're someone's intellectual property.

quiz.question: What percentage of the global seed market do the top four companies control?
